assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational framework linking collateral constraints to aggregate financial cycles, with unusually broad macroeconomic influence.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provide the central collateral mechanism; Gertler is a leading architect of the financial-accelerator extension.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been central to macro-finance research and policy analysis for decades.
uncertainties: The broad literature makes the exact division between the collateral and financial-accelerator contributions difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian work has materially changed the analysis of monetary and fiscal transmission.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are closely associated with the modern quantitative formulation and its macroeconomic applications.
assessment.maturity: The approach is now extensively used, though its prize-worthy boundaries and ultimate empirical standing remain under development.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse across a larger heterogeneous-agent macro literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection reshaped modern trade theory and empirical work on trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the pivotal originator; Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to the broader research programme.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had sustained theoretical and empirical influence over more than two decades.
uncertainties: The appropriate laureate set depends on how narrowly the contribution is defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification supplied a disciplined alternative to unwarranted point identification and changed applied econometric practice.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the indispensable intellectual originator; Tamer and Molinari made important advances in moment inequalities and implementation.
assessment.maturity: The conceptual contribution is mature and has generated a durable methodological literature.
uncertainties: The contribution's practical reach is narrower than that of some leading applied fields.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme connected taxable-income responses, administrative evidence, and optimal-tax design in a highly consequential way.
assessment.attribution: Saez is central to modern optimal-tax analysis; Slemrod and Stantcheva provide major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: The research is influential in both public-finance scholarship and policy debate.
uncertainties: Elasticity estimates and welfare conclusions remain context-dependent.
Attribution spans a large public-finance literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods created a widely used toolkit for addressing fixed effects and endogeneity in panel data.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond developed the landmark estimator, with Blundell providing the crucial system-GMM extension.
assessment.maturity: The methods are long established and broadly used across empirical economics.
uncertainties: Widespread use has also exposed finite-sample and instrument-proliferation concerns.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data transformed the measurement of intergenerational mobility and made its geographic variation salient.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman are core contributors to the linked-data research programme.
assessment.maturity: The evidence has already had substantial scholarly and public impact, though its longer-run interpretation continues to develop.
uncertainties: Causal interpretations of place-based mobility patterns remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework provided the workhorse theory for modern monetary-policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Woodford, Calvo, and Galí made defining contributions, but many additional researchers are integral to the framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework is exceptionally mature and central to monetary economics and policy institutions.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping encompasses several distinct contributions.
